items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine, Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine and Johnny Wiggs Interview, 1959-02-27
items.q: And Haley Brunus, and Georgie Brunus, and Merit Brunus, and Abby Brunus, and had Kaz Out. Oh, yeah, Jones Kaz Out. All them kids, you know, brothers, they played music. And I stood right between them and told them how to come down.

ctx.x: Jimmy Kennell. He played cornet too. He played with him too?

I was over, this was around about 1910. Somewhere along around 1910. I was in Biloxi. I had three bands in Biloxi. I had a junior band playing for the junior company. I had one for the West End and one for a volunteer. Three bands. Well, I had all kids. All youngsters ranged in Biloxi, I guess they'd say, from about 16 years down to eight. I had 14 pieces in that band. Mississippi Hook and Ladder was right across the park where we were in, what's the name, Kennedy's Hotel. The park was like here, Kennedy's Hotel…
They played all them halls, the Portuguese and the Washington of Terror, the out- I don't think- All that used to always have ordainances, you know, balls and all.

items.title: Brunies Brother Band Interview, 1957-10-19
items.q: yes i worked for jack lane over here at the fineman's day

ctx.x: . Now we have some time. Yeah, it's going all right now. If you can just tell us first, forget your name on Abby, so we know. Okay, this is Abby Brunus speaking. And now these folks are here wanting to know how I started. It's been so long, it's hard to remember. We're back there in 1908. When were you born? In 1900. And we started out, I think we were the first school band in the United States. There was only three pieces. And the three pieces consist of Emmett Rogers, George Brunus, and myself. And then we...…

. He played it on the floor like that and stuff. George had people stand on his chest. Yeah, jump on his chest. What we call that eccentric. So Henry did all that too. Henry done that before George did that. Yeah, sure. Henry was really the originator of it. Well, uh, start. I didn't get that on here. You say Henry could read a good reader, but the rest of you never did learn to read. No, none of us read outside of Henry. Henry would sit down and play first chair in a big 60-piece band.
